clue.text: Talk about American lake

parts.note: ca. is the abbreviation of circa, meaning about
Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: Someone discussing an American lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A causerie is a chatty informal essay or conversation, borrowed from French, so it is a synonym for talk.

clue.text: A fun formation in a way, for Roman birds

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the phrase meaning a way

parts.note: a, as written
via is Latin for way, as in the Appian Way

indicators.note: a formation is something put into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Roman road laid out for fun, with birds overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman birds' reads as birds of Rome, but via is also the Latin road word, so the clue's Roman flavour runs through both parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Avifauna is the bird life of a region, so the birds of Rome make up its avifauna.

clue.text: Arrangement involving Times permits unusual simultaneous deliveries

indicators.note: involving means the arrangement word wraps round the next piece

parts.note: a setup is an arrangement
x is the multiplication sign, read as times
lets means permits, allows

explanation.surface: A newspaper's licensing arrangement for odd simultaneous deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the sign X; 'involving' puts it inside SETUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Six babies born at one birth are rare simultaneous deliveries in the obstetric sense.

clue.text: Manage to hear cast in rehearsal

parts.note: to run something is to manage it

indicators.note: to hear signals a word that sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: cast means threw

explanation.surface: A director trying to hear the cast during a rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hear' makes THREW (cast) sound like THROUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-through is a practice performance of a whole piece, i.e. a rehearsal.

clue.text: Distinguished one source of gold among ten possibilities

indicators.note: among means one piece is placed inside the other
possibilities suggests the letters of the word ten in other arrangements

parts.note: a mine is one place gold comes from

explanation.surface: A prospector weighing ten possible sites for gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one source of gold' is a single phrase: a mine is one place gold comes from, not I plus a symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent describes someone notable and respected, a synonym for distinguished.

clue.text: Patriotism's a refuge for small group

indicators.note: a refuge shelters something, so the word holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Echoes Johnson's line that patriotism is the last refuge of a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside paTRIOtism; 'a refuge for' signals the concealment.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a set of three, which is a small group of people or things.

clue.text: Large portion of spaghetti served with vermouth, no longer fresh

indicators.note: a large portion means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: spaghetti is a kind of pasta
it is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A big plate of spaghetti and a vermouth that have gone stale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large portion of' drops the last A of PASTA; IT for Italian vermouth comes from the British drink gin and it.
explanation.definitionFit: Past it is an idiom for someone or something past its best, no longer fresh.

clue.text: One resorted to series of theology lectures

parts.note: RE is religious education, the school subject of religious lessons
a course is a series, as of lectures

explanation.surface: Someone attending a series of theology lectures.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (religious education) is the British school subject covering religion.
explanation.definitionFit: A recourse is a source of help that a person turns to when in need.

clue.text: Nobleman appears to spoil good party

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
a rave is a lively party

explanation.surface: An aristocrat ruins a perfectly good party.
explanation.definitionFit: A margrave was a German noble ranking as a marquis, ruler of a border territory.

clue.text: Do nothing about limiting one kind of poison

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing, so the first word goes round the next piece

parts.note: do, as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: about means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: Advice to sit idle around poison.
explanation.walkthrough: Nix is informal for nothing; 'Do' is taken literally as letters, not as the verb in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Dioxins are highly toxic chlorinated compounds, a type of poisonous chemical.

clue.text: Painter spoilt rotten when entertained by former president

indicators.note: entertained by means held inside the following piece

parts.note: Tito was president of Yugoslavia

indicators.note: spoilt signals the letters of rotten rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter thoroughly pampered by an ex-president.
explanation.walkthrough: Tito led Yugoslavia from 1953 to 1980, a staple 'former president' in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintoretto was a Venetian Renaissance painter of the sixteenth century.

clue.text: Put up regardless with dullard

definitions.meaning: to put up with something regardless

explanation.surface: Tolerating a dim companion regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means tolerating without liking, and the noun is slang for a clumsy, stupid person.

clue.text: Man involved with tigers, right?

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A circus hand who works with tigers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' mixes MAN, TIGERS and R into the answer, and the whole clue also defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringmaster directs a circus show, including its tiger acts.

clue.text: Foreign statesman needed a hand with commission

parts.note: a mitt is slang for a hand
an errand is a task or commission

explanation.surface: A diplomat requiring help with a task.
explanation.definitionFit: François Mitterrand was President of France, a statesman from the British setter's point of view foreign.

clue.text: To NASA, it's a drop in the ocean

definitions.text: To NASA, it's a drop in the ocean

parts.words: To NASA, it's a drop in the ocean
parts.note: the idiom for something trivial is read literally as a spacecraft dropping into the sea

explanation.surface: To NASA, it's trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacecraft's return by landing in the sea is literally a drop into the ocean.

clue.text: Pretend to see

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to claim or pretend and to discern something with effort.

clue.text: Great deal of medicine makes a dog seem unsteady

indicators.note: unsteady means wobbling, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A large dose of medicine leaves the dog wobbly.
explanation.definitionFit: A megadose is an unusually large dose, a great deal of medicine at once.

clue.text: Highly-reclusive sort, one time in fashion

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next piece

parts.note: style is fashion
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A hermit who was once fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I and T inside STYLE; 'Highly' hints that the hermit lived up a pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylites were ascetics who lived on top of pillars, reclusive and literally high up.

clue.text: Limit period of time in employment — not allowed to finish

parts.note: a term is a period of time

indicators.note: not finishing means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: use means employment

explanation.surface: A fixed-term job that cannot be completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not allowed to finish' cuts USE to US.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is an end point or boundary, a synonym for a limit.

clue.text: Object of ridicule on society page

parts.note: a butt is the target of jokes

explanation.surface: Someone mocked on the society page of a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'page' looks like a newspaper page but means a pageboy.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttons is a traditional name for a pageboy, from the rows of buttons on the uniform.

clue.text: Assume you'll be covered to end of life, getting pension

indicators.note: being covered means held inside the next piece

parts.note: to guess is to assume
thou is an old form of you

indicators.note: end of means the last letter

explanation.surface: Advice to insure yourself for life to get a pension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pension' looks like retirement income, but here it is the French-style boarding house; the insurance surface misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: A pension in the European sense is a boarding house, which is a lodging business.

clue.text: Strong beer, no longer a common after-dinner drink?

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
port is a fortified wine drunk after dinner

explanation.surface: A strong beer is no longer the usual drink after a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Export is a British name for a strong, full-bodied beer.

clue.text: Certainly swell, but not grand

indicators.note: but not means the following letter is removed

parts.note: a surge is a swell
G is slang for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Yes, it was great, but not grand.
explanation.definitionFit: Sure is an informal reply meaning certainly.

clue.text: Procreated with abandon? One might express disapproval

indicators.note: abandon means unrestrained wildness, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Reckless procreation draws disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: A deprecator is someone who expresses disapproval of something.

clue.text: Be speechless with emotion, deprived of heroin drug

indicators.note: deprived of means a letter is taken away

parts.note: to choke is to be unable to speak through emotion
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Emotionally overwhelmed after losing a heroin supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Coke is slang for cocaine, an illegal drug.

clue.text: A rise in value

parts.note: to mount is to rise

explanation.surface: An increase in worth.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount is a sum or quantity, so it means a value.

clue.text: Old nurse admits special knack for the afflicted

indicators.note: admits means takes inside

parts.note: SEN was a State Enrolled Nurse, a British qualification now discontinued
a trick is a special knack

explanation.surface: An old nurse with a gift for caring for the sick.
explanation.walkthrough: SEN (State Enrolled Nurse) was a former British nursing grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Stricken means badly affected by trouble or illness, so it is a synonym for afflicted.

clue.text: African girl entertains Europeans

indicators.note: entertains means holds within

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name
Danes are Europeans from Denmark

explanation.surface: A woman hosting European guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudanese means a person from Sudan, an African country.
